title: Interactive STFT Spectrogram Analyzer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Short-Time Fourier Transform
Spectrogram
Time-Frequency Resolution
Window Functions
description: A test signal built from two tones, two clicks, a chirp and noise is analyzed with the short-time Fourier transform twice, with a short and a long window. The two spectrograms share a time axis, each with the spectrum of the frame at the cursor, and cursors measure time and frequency separations.

educational.topic: Comparing short and long STFT windows on a multi-component signal
learningObjectives: Compare spectrograms of one signal made with a short and a long window
Predict from the window length whether two tones or two clicks will be separated
Measure time and frequency separations on a spectrogram with cursors
Justify a choice of window length, window type and hop size for a given signal
prerequisites: The DFT, bin spacing and window functions

controls.label: Click a spectrogram to place the time and frequency cursor; point elsewhere to read the separation from the cursor

equations: X[m, k] = sum over n of x[n + m H] w[n] e^(-j 2 pi k n / N)
time span of the window = N / fs, bin spacing = fs / N, product = 1
two impulses tau seconds apart have a spectrum with ripples every 1 / tau hertz
assumptions: fs = 8000 Hz; the signal is 1 s long and 250 to 750 ms and 0 to 2000 Hz are displayed
Tones have amplitude 1, clicks are single samples of amplitude 8, the chirp rises from 1100 to 1900 Hz over the full second, and the noise has standard deviation 0.2
The FFT length equals the window length (no zero-padding)
Levels are scaled so that a steady bin-centred sinusoid of amplitude 1 reads 0 dB; the colour scale spans 60 dB

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison of two analyses of the same signal, with a test signal designed so that each window fails at one task
keyQuestions: Which window separates the tones, which separates the clicks, and why not both?
How many bins apart must two tones be to appear as two lines?
What does the hop size change, and what does it leave unchanged?
commonMisconceptions: There is one best window length for every signal
A smaller hop size improves time resolution
Information that a spectrogram does not show has been destroyed
assessmentOpportunities: Tabulate, for each window length, whether the tones and the clicks are separated
Measure the ripple spacing in a frame that contains both clicks and relate it to the click spacing
